title: Identity controls: wireframes, tradeoffs, and backlog
content:
Summary:
Working notes and lightweight wireframe writeups for an "identity controls" area in Console that groups RBAC, API keys, and service accounts plus a compact audit-log view. Goal: reduce support churn for key management, make team-level least-privilege patterns discoverable, and provide an audit surface that helps debugging without noise.

High-level constraints and principles (narrow):
- Single-source UI for identity tasks (create key, rotate, assign role, simulate) but split modes for admin vs member.
- Default templates first: make the 80% easiest (read-only, invoke-only, infra) and allow custom roles as advanced.
- Visibility: audit log must show context (request header, model, route) without exposing secrets.
- Don’t reinvent policy language: expose human-readable intent + preview of API impact (dry-run simulation).

Wireframe notes (sketch -> components -> microcopy):
1) Identity dashboard (landing)
   - Top: team selector + quick-actions: "Create API key", "Create service account", "Audit recent activity".
   - Panels: Active keys (table), Service accounts (card list), Roles & templates (list), Recent security events (compact timeline).
   - Table cols for Active keys: label, owner, scope (comma list), last used, rotate (CTA), status. Inline kebab for revoke/duplicate/download (download only once).
   - Microcopy: under keys table: "API keys can be rotated. Downloads are only available at creation for security reasons."

2) Create API key flow (3-step modal)
   - Step 1: Name + owner + TTL (optional) + template dropdown (Recommended: "Invoke-only", "Billing-report", "Admin-ops").
   - Step 2: Scopes granularization UI: toggle model-invoke, embeddings:create, billing:read, keys:manage. Show estimated blast radius badge (low/medium/high).
   - Step 3: Review & copy key (one-time). Show link to rotate schedule and recommended rotation cadence. Offer HSM-backed option (enterprise only) with note "rotate via KMS if enabled".
   - Notes: show checkbox "Send key to service account" for infra templates (auto-create service account + bind).

3) Service account card details
   - Expandable card with: description, linked keys, impersonation toggle, bound roles, last impersonated by, allowed projects.  CTA: "Create key for service account".
   - Modal: impersonation demo with exact curl snippet and placeholders for ephemeral token TTL.

4) Role templates & role editor
   - Left: built-in templates w/ short intent, right: role editor (allow lists of granular permissions).
   - Preview panel: "What this role allows a user to do" with example API calls and a dry-run switch to simulate against a selected team route.

5) Audit log compact view (new)
   - Default: compact timeline with search bar + high-cardinality filters (actor, resource, action, model, ip). Each item: time, actor, short verb, resource, badge (success/fail), link to contextual pane.
   - Contextual pane (right slide-over): full event JSON (collapsed by default) plus related events clustering (e.g., same key used across 3 routes in 10m).
   - Retention UI: warn when older events will be truncated; include "export window" CTA to request exports.

Tradeoffs discussed (open):
- Show key scopes inline vs separate detail page: inline improves discoverability but risks cluttering the keys table. Current lean: show scopes truncated, full scopes on hover/expand.
- Template proliferation: provide 4 templates + team-create option; avoid freeform templates by default.
- Dry-run simulation: powerful but needs infra hook (rate-limited). Start with limited simulator that only checks RBAC decision graph, not full call path.

Backlog grooming (short list, prioritized):
- P0: Create API key modal MVP (3 screens, copy + one-time download) - estimate 5d frontend + 3d backend for key lifecycle endpoints - ticket PROJ-3187.
- P0: Keys table + rotate/revoke actions + one-time download UX - 3d frontend + 2d API.
- P1: Role templates UI + preview/dry-run toggle (RBAC engine integration) - 8d.
- P1: Service account card + create key for SA + impersonation snippet - 5d.
- P2: Audit log compact timeline + contextual pane + export CTA (basic filters) - 6d.
- P2: HSM/KMS option visible in modal (enterprise gating) - 2d infra + 2d UI.

Acceptance criteria (for P0 items):
- User can create a key, view it once, and see it listed with correct metadata.
- Rotate action invalidates previous token and surfaces new key only at creation.
- Revoke marks key as disabled and prevents all subsequent operations in integration tests.

Unresolved questions / decisions to escalate:
- Who signs off on default template names and blast-radius labels? (Product + Security)
- Should we expose model-level scopes (e.g., model:rw) now or wait until we have fine-grained routing? (Engineering lead preference: postpone).
- Default retention for audit log and export SLA for large customers—product to confirm with SRE/cost.
- How to present legacy keys that predate scopes? Migration UX options: auto-map to broad scope + prompt owner to review vs lock-and-force-rotate.

Notes to eng (implementation hints):
- Backend: need endpoints for dry-run evaluation (rbac/eval) and for key usage last_seen. Rate-limit dry-run to 1/second per org.
- UX: make key downloads ephemeral (show masked example in UI post-creation). Prevent copy-paste auto-save by detecting clipboard action? (note: privacy/legal investigation).
- Telemetry: instrument events for create/rotate/revoke and include template_id.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Align on template naming: set up 30-min sync with Security (Ravi + Maya) next Tuesday.
- Spike: 2d proof-of-concept for dry-run RBAC eval (Elliot) — report back with API contract.
- Design: produce 2 medium-fidelity screens for create-key modal and audit timeline by EOW (Sofia).

Quick sketches (textual):
- "Compact audit item" -> "2025-02-10 18:23 - maya.chen@redwood - invoke - route:/v1/generate - model:gpt-redwood-13b - ✓" (click opens slide-over).
- "Key row" -> "label: mobile-prod | owner: infra-team | scopes: model:invoke, embeddings:create | last used: 2025-02-09 | actions: rotate, revoke, details".

User scenarios to validate in usability testing:
- Platform engineer rotates an API key used by a backend job and verifies the job fails then recovers after swapping secret in deploy.
- Product manager creates an invoke-only key for analytics ingestion and tries to use it for a billing call (should be blocked).
- Security auditor searches for failed impersonation attempts and exports the one-week window.

References & tickets mentioned in doc:
- PROJ-3187 (Create key modal)
- PROJ-3201 (Audit compact view spike)
- CONFLUENCE: https://redwood.atl/confluence/identity-controls-draft

Misc notes / personal TODOs:
- Add copy variant for SSO orgs where keys are forbidden by policy.
- Check legal on whether we can log full request headers in audit exports (PII risk).

End of doc.
